findings.claim: The diff swaps Tailwind v3 (with postcss/autoprefixer/tailwindcss-animate) for Tailwind v4 (@tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, tailwindcss 4.3.3, tw-animate-css) but contains no corresponding changes to vite.config.ts, any CSS entry file, or any tailwind config, so the existing PostCSS-based build (`@tailwind` directives, config requiring tailwindcss-animate) will fail or render unstyled.
findings.evidence: package.json hunks remove `"tailwindcss-animate": "^1.0.7"`, `"autoprefixer": "^10.4.24"`, `"postcss": "^8.5.6"`, `"tailwindcss": "^3.4.19"` and add `"@tailwindcss/vite": "4.3.3"`, `"tailwindcss": "4.3.3"`, `"tw-animate-css"`; no hunk in the diff wires `@tailwindcss/vite` into `frontend/vite.config.ts` (present in file tree) or migrates CSS to `@import "tailwindcss"`. The enhanced-thread.tsx hunks also silently depend on new v4 tokens (`var(--color-surface)`, `var(--color-cyan)`) that no diff hunk defines.
findings.suggested_fix: Either include the vite config + CSS migration (add the @tailwindcss/vite plugin, replace @tailwind directives with @import "tailwindcss", port tailwindcss-animate usage to tw-animate-css, define --color-surface/--color-cyan) in this change, or split the Tailwind v4 migration out of the markdown-pipeline diff entirely.

findings.claim: `@radix-ui/react-icons` is removed from dependencies with no hunk removing its imports anywhere in the source, so any remaining importer produces a module-not-found build/typecheck failure.
findings.evidence: package.json hunk deletes `"@radix-ui/react-icons": "^1.3.2"` and the diff contains no frontend/src changes removing usage of that package (the file tree does not let one confirm zero importers, and the deleted enhanced-markdown-text.tsx did not import it).
findings.suggested_fix: Grep the frontend for `@radix-ui/react-icons` and include the codemod to lucide-react in this diff, or restore the dependency.

findings.claim: The shared `code` component no longer distinguishes block code from inline code (the old `useIsMarkdownCodeBlock` branching was deleted), so fenced code blocks receive the inline pill styling (`rounded-md bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5`) inside the padded `pre`, and hljs syntax highlighting is silently dropped while `highlight.js` remains a dependency.
findings.evidence: Deleted enhanced-markdown-text.tsx contained `EnhancedCodeBlock` using `useIsMarkdownCodeBlock` and hljs highlighting; the new markdown-components.tsx has a single `code: ({ className, ...props }) => <code className={cn("rounded-md bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[0.85em]", ...)} />` applied to both inline and block code, and package.json still lists `"highlight.js": "^11.10.0"`. Criterion 3.1 only authorizes moving the presentation map, not removing highlighting.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore block/inline differentiation (e.g., via node.position or a pre/code pair check) and either re-implement highlighting in the shared map or explicitly remove highlight.js and document the regression.

findings.claim: All components spread `{...props}` onto DOM elements, but react-markdown passes a `node` property to components in explicit-source mode, producing React unknown-prop warnings and potential invalid attributes on every rendered element in the Skills preview path.
findings.evidence: markdown-bubble.tsx passes `components={markdownComponents}` directly to `<ReactMarkdown>`; react-markdown v9+ invokes components with `{ node, ... }` and the components here destructure only `className` before spreading the rest (e.g., `h1: ({ className, ...props }) => <h1 ... {...props} />`).
findings.suggested_fix: Destructure and discard `node` in each component (`({ node, className, ...props })`) or wrap the map for the ReactMarkdown path.

findings.claim: Every test exercises only the explicit-`source` ReactMarkdown path; the assistant-ui context mode (`MarkdownTextPrimitive` with the same rehypeChain and `defer`) has zero coverage, so a prop-forwarding or ordering failure in the actual chat rendering path ships untested despite criterion 4.1.
findings.evidence: All seven tests render `<MarkdownBubble source={...} />`; none mounts `MarkdownBubble` inside an assistant-ui message-part context or asserts that `MarkdownTextPrimitive` applies `rehypePlugins`/`remarkPlugins` in the required raw→sanitize→katex order.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test rendering the context mode (via assistant-ui test harness or a MarkdownTextPrimitive mock) asserting the chain order and XSS stripping hold there too.

findings.claim: `dompurify` is added as a runtime dependency to satisfy criterion 1.2 but is never imported anywhere in the diff; sanitization is implemented entirely via rehype-sanitize, leaving a dead dependency in the production bundle graph.
findings.evidence: package.json adds `"dompurify": "^3.4.13"` under dependencies; no file in the diff imports `dompurify`, and sanitize-schema.ts/rehype-chain.ts use only rehype-sanitize.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove dompurify (and amend criterion 1.2's evidence) or document the concrete consumer that requires it.

findings.claim: The `hr` component drops all props and renders an empty `<div className="my-5 h-3" role="separator" />`, removing the visible rule and any sanitized attributes the old `<hr>` carried.
findings.evidence: Old map: `hr: ({ className, ...props }) => <hr className={cn("my-4 border-border/30", className)} {...props} />`; new map: `hr: () => <div className="my-5 h-3" role="separator" />`.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep an `<hr>` (or give the div a visible border) and forward className/props.
